To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed distribution-free approach is a useful tool for combining multiple diagnostic markers and that it can be applied in the presence of covariate effects and smoothness assumptions.

(1) the proposed distribution-free method optimizes the partial area under the ROC curves for the pancreatic and prostate cancer data; (2) the proposed distribution free method performs better than LDA and logistic regression when data are multivariatetnormal; and (3) logistic regression performs better than L DA when data are not multivariate normal, but it is outperformed by the distribution free method.

(i) a distribution-free method for optimizing area under the ROC is more accurate than logistic regression and linear discriminant analysis; (ii) a smooth distribution-free method for optimized partial area under the ROC can be applied to accommodate some reasonable smooth assumptions, to incorporate covariate effects, and to focus on a particular region of the ROC; (iii) the methods are illustrated on two real data examples involving cancer markers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for optimizing diagnostic accuracy when combining multiple diagnostic tests.
developing methods for combining information from multiple diagnostic tests in order to improve the accuracy of disease diagnosis.
developing and evaluating methods for optimizing the diagnostic accuracy of multiple tests.

the proposed nonparametric approach is the best choice for optimizing diagnostic accuracy in general.
